statement: Every unit-distance graph in the Euclidean plane is 3-colorable, so the chromatic number of the plane is 3.
definitions: A unit-distance graph is a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane with an edge between two points exactly when their distance is 1; 3-colorable = proper vertex coloring with 3 colors; refuting the first clause suffices.
ground_truth_witness: The Moser spindle: the 7 points O=(0,0), A1=(sqrt(3)/2, 1/2), A2=(sqrt(3)/2, -1/2), T1=(sqrt(3), 0), B1=(5*sqrt(3)/12 - sqrt(11)/12, 5/12 + sqrt(33)/12), B2=(5*sqrt(3)/12 + sqrt(11)/12, -5/12 + sqrt(33)/12), T2=(5*sqrt(3)/6, sqrt(33)/6). (B1, B2, T2 are the rotation of A1, A2, T1 by the angle with cos = 5/6, sin = sqrt(11)/6.) Exactly 11 of the 21 pairwise distances equal 1, namely O-A1, O-A2, A1-A2, A1-T1, A2-T1, O-B1, O-B2, B1-B2, B1-T2, B2-T2, T1-T2; the resulting 7-vertex 11-edge unit-distance graph has no proper 3-coloring, so its chromatic number is 4 and the chromatic number of the plane is at least 4.
